Paper_Metadata.Paper_Title: High temperature performances of abradable sealing coating for ceramic matrix composites

Composition_Info.Alloy_Name_Raw: ZC20 bi-layer ASC: Si bond layer + YSZ-20 vol% CaF2 top layer
Composition_Info.Note: Top layer nominal composition is YSZ-20 vol% CaF2. Exact yttria content in YSZ was not reported. Coating system is a bi-layer ASC with Si bond layer on a SiC/CMC-type substrate for oxidation and thermal shock testing; wear tests were performed on graphite-disc-supported coatings.

Process_Info.Process_Category: Powder mixing, spray drying, pre-sintering, and APS bi-layer coating deposition

Process_Text.original: Commercially available YSZ (Oerlikon Metco Surface Technology Co., Ltd., Switzerland) and CaF2 (Shanghai Aladdin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd., China) were used as plasma spray powders. The YSZ-20 vol% CaF2 powders were mixed in alcohol, spray dried by spray drier (LPG-5, Wuxi Chenying Machinery Technology Co., Ltd, China) and sintered using a furnace (KSL170, Hefei Kejing Material Technology Co., Ltd., China) at 1100 °C for the fabrication of coatings. The Si bonding and top layers were deposited by the APS system (A-2000, Sulzer Metco AG, Switzerland) and the parameters can be found in references [35,36].
Process_Text.simplified: Commercial YSZ and CaF2 were mixed to 20 vol% CaF2, spray dried, pre-sintered at 1100 °C, and deposited as a Si-bonded bi-layer coating by APS. Detailed APS spraying parameters were not reported in this paper and were referenced to prior work.

Process_Info.Equipment: Spray drier LPG-5 (Wuxi Chenying Machinery Technology Co., Ltd., China); furnace KSL170 (Hefei Kejing Material Technology Co., Ltd., China); APS system A-2000 (Sulzer Metco AG, Switzerland); XRD D8 ADVANCE (Bruker, Germany); SEM Magellan 400 (FEI, USA); Rockwell hardness gauge (SHIMADZU, Japan); tribometer UMT-2 (Bruker, Germany); probe profiler DektakXTL (Bruker, Germany); thermal shock furnace RZR1600 (Shanghai Junke Instrument Technology Co., Ltd., China)

Microstructure_Text.original: The ZC20 powder was mainly composed of tetragonal ZrO2 and CaF2 phases. The main phases of the ZC20 coating were the same as the powder. The feedstock powders were uniformly distributed in terms of particle size and showed spherical and agglomerated shapes, which is the typical shape of spray-granulating suitable for APS technology. The surface of the coatings was in good molten state, and the molten particles were spread out and overlapped each other on the surface of the substrate, forming completely melted and partially melted regions. From the cross-sectional morphologies of the coatings, few pores and microcracks existed inside the coatings. There were different contrast differences within the coatings. Ca and F elements presented a strip-like aggregation, which was mainly distributed in the deep gray region, indicating that CaF2 was successfully deposited into the coating. More microcracks and micropores existed around it, which might be due to the volatilization of CaF2 during the spraying process. After oxidation at 1100 °C for 100 h, apparent microcracks and a large number of pores were present inside the coating. A TGO layer with a thickness of about 15 μm formed at the Si bond layer, and a new CaSiO3-rich layer appeared between TGO and the coating. After thermal shock, vertical penetrating cracks and interfacial cracks were observed.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: As-sprayed ZC20 showed a dense APS lamellar coating with fully and partially melted splats, few pores and microcracks, and strip-like CaF2-rich regions. After oxidation, microcracks, pores, a ~15 μm TGO layer, and an interfacial CaSiO3 layer formed. Thermal shock generated penetrating and interfacial cracks.

Composition_Info.Alloy_Name_Raw: MC20 bi-layer ASC: Si bond layer + Yb2SiO5-20 vol% CaF2 top layer
Composition_Info.Note: Top layer nominal composition is Yb2SiO5-20 vol% CaF2. The Yb2SiO5 powder was synthesized by solid-state reaction before composite powder preparation.

Process_Info.Process_Category: Yb2SiO5 powder synthesis, powder mixing, spray drying, pre-sintering, and APS bi-layer coating deposition

Process_Text.original: Yb2SiO5 powder was prepared by solid-state reaction, using SiO2 (Slno pharm Chemical Reagent Co., Ltd., China) and Yb2O3 (Shanghai Heli Rare Earth Material Co., Ltd., China) as raw materials. The Yb2SiO5-20 vol% CaF2 powders were mixed in alcohol, spray dried by spray drier (LPG-5, Wuxi Chenying Machinery Technology Co., Ltd, China) and sintered using a furnace (KSL170, Hefei Kejing Material Technology Co., Ltd., China) at 1100 °C for the fabrication of coatings. The Si bonding and top layers were deposited by the APS system (A-2000, Sulzer Metco AG, Switzerland) and the parameters can be found in references [35,36].
Process_Text.simplified: Yb2SiO5 feedstock was synthesized by solid-state reaction from SiO2 and Yb2O3, then blended with 20 vol% CaF2, spray dried, pre-sintered at 1100 °C, and deposited as a Si-bonded APS bi-layer coating. Detailed APS spraying parameters were not reported in this paper.

Process_Info.Equipment: Spray drier LPG-5 (Wuxi Chenying Machinery Technology Co., Ltd., China); furnace KSL170 (Hefei Kejing Material Technology Co., Ltd., China); APS system A-2000 (Sulzer Metco AG, Switzerland); XRD D8 ADVANCE (Bruker, Germany); SEM Magellan 400 (FEI, USA); Rockwell hardness gauge (SHIMADZU, Japan); tribometer UMT-2 (Bruker, Germany); probe profiler DektakXTL (Bruker, Germany); thermal shock furnace RZR1600 (Shanghai Junke Instrument Technology Co., Ltd., China)

Microstructure_Text.original: The MC20 powder was mainly composed of Yb2SiO5 and CaF2 phases. In contrast to powders, the MC20 coating also contained the Yb2O3 phase. The feedstock powders were spherical and agglomerated. The surface of the coating was in good molten state and the cross-sectional morphologies showed few pores and microcracks inside the coatings. Different contrast differences could be attributed to different CaF2 content and decomposition of Yb2SiO5. After oxidation at 1100 °C for 100 h, significant regions of intensive porosity were present inside the coating, and different regions had apparent contrast differences. Region 1 was mainly Yb2O3, region 2 was Yb2SiO5, and regions 3 and 4 were CaF2-reacted regions yielding Ca2Yb8(SiO4)6O2. The Si bonding layer reacted to form a TGO layer with a thickness of about 20 μm. After oxidation at 1200 °C and 1300 °C for 100 h, penetrating cracks, horizontal cracks, intensive porosity regions, and finally a porous reaction layer in the upper region were observed. After thermal shock, vertical penetrating cracks and interfacial cracks formed.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: As-sprayed MC20 was a dense APS lamellar coating based on Yb2SiO5 with CaF2 and a secondary Yb2O3 phase. Oxidation produced Ca2Yb8(SiO4)6O2 and a ~20 μm TGO layer, while higher-temperature oxidation generated penetrating and horizontal cracks and a porous upper reaction layer. Thermal shock caused penetrating and interfacial cracks.

Composition_Info.Alloy_Name_Raw: YC20 bi-layer ASC: Si bond layer + Yb2Si2O7-20 vol% CaF2 top layer
Composition_Info.Note: Top layer nominal composition is Yb2Si2O7-20 vol% CaF2. The Yb2Si2O7 powder was synthesized by solid-state reaction before composite powder preparation.

Process_Info.Process_Category: Yb2Si2O7 powder synthesis, powder mixing, spray drying, pre-sintering, and APS bi-layer coating deposition

Process_Text.original: Yb2Si2O7 powder was prepared by solid-state reaction, using SiO2 (Slno pharm Chemical Reagent Co., Ltd., China) and Yb2O3 (Shanghai Heli Rare Earth Material Co., Ltd., China) as raw materials. The Yb2Si2O7-20 vol% CaF2 powders were mixed in alcohol, spray dried by spray drier (LPG-5, Wuxi Chenying Machinery Technology Co., Ltd, China) and sintered using a furnace (KSL170, Hefei Kejing Material Technology Co., Ltd., China) at 1100 °C for the fabrication of coatings. The Si bonding and top layers were deposited by the APS system (A-2000, Sulzer Metco AG, Switzerland) and the parameters can be found in references [35,36].
Process_Text.simplified: Yb2Si2O7 feedstock was synthesized by solid-state reaction from SiO2 and Yb2O3, then blended with 20 vol% CaF2, spray dried, pre-sintered at 1100 °C, and deposited as a Si-bonded APS bi-layer coating. Detailed APS spraying parameters were not reported in this paper.

Process_Info.Equipment: Spray drier LPG-5 (Wuxi Chenying Machinery Technology Co., Ltd., China); furnace KSL170 (Hefei Kejing Material Technology Co., Ltd., China); APS system A-2000 (Sulzer Metco AG, Switzerland); XRD D8 ADVANCE (Bruker, Germany); SEM Magellan 400 (FEI, USA); Rockwell hardness gauge (SHIMADZU, Japan); tribometer UMT-2 (Bruker, Germany); probe profiler DektakXTL (Bruker, Germany); thermal shock furnace RZR1600 (Shanghai Junke Instrument Technology Co., Ltd., China)

Microstructure_Text.original: The YC20 powder was mainly composed of Yb2Si2O7 and CaF2 phases. In contrast to powders, the YC20 coating additionally possessed the Yb2SiO5 phase. The feedstock powders were spherical and agglomerated. The surface of the coating was in good molten state and the cross-sectional morphologies showed few pores and microcracks inside the coatings. Different contrast differences could be attributed to the different CaF2 content and the decomposition of Yb2Si2O7. After oxidation at 1100 °C for 100 h, more pores were observed inside the coating. Regions 5 and 6 mainly consisted of Ca2Yb8(SiO4)6O2 generated by reaction of CaF2 with Yb2Si2O7, and the coating/bond layer bonding was excellent. The Si bonding layer was oxidized to form a TGO layer with a thickness of about 20 μm, and significant microcracks existed inside the TGO. After oxidation at 1200 °C and 1300 °C for 100 h, the coating remained structurally intact macroscopically; penetrating cracks were seen at 1200 °C, and at 1300 °C a significant number of pores formed by the reaction were uniformly distributed throughout the coating, with horizontal cracks at the interface between the bonding layer and the substrate. After thermal shock, many microcracks and interfacial cracks were present but no large-area spalling occurred.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: As-sprayed YC20 was a dense APS lamellar coating based on Yb2Si2O7 with CaF2 and some Yb2SiO5 secondary phase. Oxidation produced Ca2Yb8(SiO4)6O2 and a ~20 μm TGO layer, while higher-temperature oxidation created distributed pores and some cracking but preserved overall integrity. Thermal shock generated microcracks and interfacial cracks without large-area spalling.
